skills.name: Equivalent ratios
skills.description: Scaling both parts of a ratio by the same factor.

skills.name: Sharing in a ratio
skills.description: Splitting a total into ratio shares.

RAT_ADDITIVE.label: Adds the same amount to both parts instead of multiplying
RAT_ADDITIVE.explanation: Goes from 2 : 3 to 6 : 7 by adding 4 to both parts.

RAT_SHARE_EQUAL.label: Splits the total in half instead of in the ratio
RAT_SHARE_EQUAL.explanation: Gives each person ₹15 when ₹30 is shared 2 : 3.

RAT_DIVIDE_BY_PART.label: Divides the total by one part of the ratio
RAT_DIVIDE_BY_PART.explanation: Works out ₹30 ÷ 2 for a 2 : 3 share, forgetting there are 5 shares.

questions.prompt: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour for every 3 cups of milk. How many cups of milk go with 6 cups of flour?
hints: A ratio stays the same when you MULTIPLY both parts by the same number.
Find how many times bigger the new amount is, then multiply the other part by that.

questions.prompt: ₹30 is shared between Asha and Ben in the ratio 2 : 3. How much does Asha get (in ₹)?
hints: Add the parts of the ratio to find how many equal shares there are.
Divide the total by the number of shares, then multiply by each part.

equivalent_ratios.title: Equivalent ratios
equivalent_ratios.big_idea: A ratio compares amounts by multiplication. To keep a recipe tasting the same, both amounts must be multiplied by the same number, not increased by the same amount.
steps: Find the scale factor: new amount ÷ old amount.
Multiply the other part by the same factor.
Check: the new ratio simplifies back to the old one.
equivalent_ratios.sense_check: 2 flour : 3 milk. Tripling to 6 flour needs 9 milk. Adding 4 to both (6 : 7) would change the taste.

worked_examples.prompt: 2 flour for 3 milk. Milk for 6 flour?

sharing_in_ratio.title: Sharing in a ratio
sharing_in_ratio.big_idea: In the ratio 2 : 3 the total is split into 2 + 3 = 5 equal shares. One person gets 2 of them, the other 3. It is not split in half.
steps: Add the ratio parts to get the number of shares.
Divide the total by the number of shares.
Check: the amounts add up to the total.
sharing_in_ratio.sense_check: ₹30 in 2 : 3 gives ₹12 and ₹18. They add to 30, and 12 : 18 simplifies to 2 : 3.
